candidates.title: LAPA: Log-Domain Prediction-Driven Dynamic Sparsity Accelerator for Transformer Model
candidates.venue: Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference
candidates.abstract: Attention-based Transformers have revolutionized natural language processing (NLP) and shown strong performance in computer vision (CV) tasks. However, as the input sequence varies, the computational bottlenecks in Transformer models exhibit dynamic behavior across stages, which calls for a cross-stage sparse acceleration strategy. Unfortunately, most existing sparse Transformer approaches are single-stage based, and their sparsity prediction mechanisms lead to significant power overhead when applied across multiple stages. To this end, this paper proposes a log-domain attention prediction algorithmarchitecture co-design, named LAPA. First, an asymmetric leading one computing (ALOC) scheme is designed to eliminate expensive multiplications. Next, a mixed-precision multi-round shifting accumulation (MRSA) mechanism is further proposed to mitigate the accumulation overhead. A data-feature dependent filter (DDF) strategy is designed to work in concert with the MRSA process. Finally, an elaborate accelerator is designed to translate the theoretical enhancement into practical hardware improvement. Experimental results show that LAPA achieves $3.52 \times, 3.24 \times$ and $2.79 \times$ higher energy efficiency than the state-of-the-art (SOTA) works Spatten, Sanger and FACT, respectively.
candidates.reason: log領域の注意予測とALOC・MRSAにより複数段階のTransformer計算ボトルネックを動的スパース化するハードウェアアクセラレータLAPAで、エネルギー効率を上げる推論加速の直接貢献。

candidates.title: Rethinking Compression: Reduced Order Modelling of Latent Features in Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Due to the substantial scale of Large Language Models (LLMs), the direct application of conventional compression methodologies proves impractical. The computational demands associated with even minimal gradient updates present challenges, particularly on consumer-grade hardware. This paper introduces an innovative approach for the parametric and practical compression of LLMs based on reduced order modelling, which entails low-rank decomposition within the feature space and re-parameterization in the weight space. Notably, this compression technique operates in a layer-wise manner, obviating the need for a GPU device and enabling the compression of billion-scale models within stringent constraints of both memory and time. Our method represents a significant advancement in model compression by leveraging matrix decomposition, demonstrating superior efficacy compared to the prevailing state-of-the-art structured pruning method.
candidates.reason: 潜在特徴の低ランク分解と重み再パラメータ化による層単位のLLM圧縮で、GPUなしでも大規模モデルを圧縮できるモデル圧縮の直接貢献。

candidates.title: SOA: A Sparsity-Oriented Activation on Sub-layers of FFN of Transformers
candidates.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
candidates.abstract: Since the invention of Transformers, attention-based models have been widely used in machine translation, language understanding, and image processing. However, performance of Transformers comes at cost of significant large computation and memory requirements. Sparsification is a feasible solution to the above problems. In this paper, We propose an new approach called SOA that inserts truncated activation functions into sublayers of FFN to introduce new levels of sparsity. The introduction of the new activation functions can reduce the number of active activations and enable sparse matrix multiplications in following FFN layers. To address the problem of the accuracy degradation caused by the inserted activation functions, we employ fine-tuning to retain accuracy. Our experiments show that for BERT on GLUE datasets, with almost no accuracy degradation(average 0.045%), SOA can produce the average sparsity 60%,and reduce 31.5% of total computation for the entire Transformer, and can save 19% memory space by using run-length coding.
candidates.reason: FFNサブレイヤへ切り捨て活性化を挿入して活性化スパース性を高め、BERTで計算量31.5%・メモリ19%削減を示すTransformer推論計算削減の貢献。

candidates.title: FastForward Pruning: Efficient LLM Pruning via Single-Step Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Pruning is an effective method for compressing Large Language Models, but finding an optimal, non-uniform layer-wise sparsity allocation remains a key challenge. While heuristic methods are fast but yield suboptimal performance, more powerful search-based approaches like Reinforcement Learning are often hindered by prohibitive computational costs on large-scale models. To overcome this efficiency barrier, we propose FastForward Pruning. Its core is a decoupled, single-step RL framework that separates policy optimization from the complex budget satisfaction problem. Such a decoupling is crucial for efficiently searching the vast policy space of LLMs. This curriculum-based strategy begins with low-cost, simple tasks and gradually increases in complexity, significantly reducing the search's computational overhead. Evaluated on the LLaMA, Mistral, and OPT model families, our framework discovers pruning policies that achieve superior performance over strong heuristic baselines. Crucially, when compared to other search-based algorithms, our method achieves competitive or superior results at a fraction of the computational cost, demonstrating a clear advantage in search efficiency.
candidates.reason: 単一ステップ強化学習とカリキュラムで層別スパース率を探索するFastForward Pruningにより、LLM pruning政策探索の計算コストを下げる圧縮の直接貢献。
